## Fix

**`redact-claude` no longer erases a whole turn when a command removes its own working directory.** A Bash call such as `git worktree remove` run inside the worktree reported the removed path as `cwd`. The existing-directory guard then blocked the result and erased every output line.

An absolute `cwd` that no longer exists now resolves to its nearest existing ancestor. These still fail closed:
- a relative, empty, non-string or non-directory `cwd`;
- a vanished `cwd` spelled with `.` or `..`;
- one whose walk meets a dangling symlink or an unreadable entry;
- one seen with `HOME` unset.

Trust is still judged for the vanished path, so the result is never looser than what the original path would have allowed:
- the ancestor's own layer outside `HOME` is not discovered;
- the missing path is the workspace boundary when no repository sits above the ancestor;
- a layer that a surrounding repository would drop fails closed.

Upgrade: `brew upgrade vshuraeff/tap/sekretbarilo`.
